newsitem.title: USA: Balanced budget key to avoid instability - Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Balanced budget key to avoid instability - Greenspan.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Tuesday urged Congress and President Clinton to work toward an agreement to balance the budget, saying it was key to the stability of the U.S. economy.

"As far as I'm concerned, while it is terribly important to move to balance (in the budget) by the year 2002, it is essentially a prerequisite to fend off what is a serious, destabilizing fiscal situation," Greenspan said in testimony to the House Budget Committee.
During the question-and-answer session of the testimony, the Fed Chairman said curbing spending on entitlement programs was particularly crucial.
"Unless you do that, none of those programs will prevail because they will become utterly unfinanceable and what will occur is that interest will eat up the whole budget," he added.
